A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ACORD study, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–F. All 24 corresponding pages, including figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original retrieval evaluations, fine-tuning results and query-format experiments in Section 4, Figure 2 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v4 retains the original retrieval evaluations, fine-tuning results and query-format experiments in Section 4, Figure 2 and Appendices D–E.

M1.justification: The retrieval/reranking procedures and MiniLM cross-encoder fine-tuning objective remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix F.2. No algorithmic component or procedure is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine-category ACORD contract-clause corpus and 114 queries. Appendix E retains the same change-of-control and as-is query-format scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and D-3–D-5 retain identical comparator membership, including BM25, MiniLM, OpenAI embeddings, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini and Llama models. No comparator is added, removed or replaced within corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: The 45%/5%/50% query-level split, top-100 retrieval before reranking, evaluation metrics and fine-tuning grid remain unchanged. Appendix E also retains the same query-format evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The fine-tuning comparisons, category analyses, pointwise-versus-pairwise comparisons and query-format sensitivity experiments are unchanged in Figure 2 and Appendices D–E. Table 1 retains the same attorney-annotated drafting example.

E5.justification: Appendix F.2 reports validation-score averaging over three runs in both versions. Table C-2 retains the same descriptive statistics, and no uncertainty-reporting practice, confidence interval or significance test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains BM25 with GPT-4o at 76.9% NDCG@5 and 79.7% NDCG@10; Tables D-1–D-5 and E-2 are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definition and Appendix F.1 formulas for NDCG and normalized star-precision are mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contribution and novelty claims for an expert-annotated contract-clause retrieval benchmark. Claims about promising performance and substantial remaining room for improvement are unchanged.

C2.justification: Sections 5 and 7 retain the same interpretations concerning query context, ranking quality and pointwise reranking. Limitations concerning extracted-clause scope, subjective annotations, public contracts and English/U.S. applicability are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A, C and F retain the same annotation instructions, data-format conventions, hyperparameters, RTX A6000 hardware and runtimes. Code/data availability statements and access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning relative to contract extraction, legal reasoning and case-law retrieval. No substantive citation or positioning change occurs.

P1.justification: v4 corrects an author email typo, updates the version/date stamp and replaces cross-reference wording such as Appendix C.3 with Section C.3. The narrative, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Small typography and line-wrapping adjustments accompany the cross-reference edits, including reflow of the Table 3 caption. Figure and table designs, contents and placements remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 preserves the scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations of v3, including all appendices. The email correction and small cross-reference and typesetting edits do not materially alter the paper's overall quality.
